transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-15
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel, Carlos Mendez (Redwood); Tom Briggs, Maya Singh, Oliver Park (Nebula Finance)

[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Aisha, AE at Redwood. Carlos from our SE team is with me. How's it going over on your side?
[00:07] Tom: Hey Aisha, hey Carlos. Good, busy quarter but excited to take a look. Maya and Oliver are on the line to really dig into observability and debugging flows.
[00:14] Aisha: Awesome. Quick agenda - we'll do a Console walkthrough: tracing, error analysis, request logs and then demo a typical debugging workflow. Save time at the end for Qs and next steps. Sound good?
[00:21] Maya: Yep that sounds great.
[00:24] Carlos: Cool, jumping in. First slide - high level tracing in the Console. We surface per-request traces, model latency breakdowns, kernel-level timing where available (note: some kernel names may be abbreviated in the UI).
[00:36] [00:30] Carlos: So here's a trace sample - you can see request start, routing decision, KV cache hit/miss, compilation step, and then token generation. We annotate where batching occurred and any fallback to model variants.
[00:48] Maya: Quick Q - will the trace show when a request is rerouted from Hosted to Dedicated or to a fallback model?
[00:53] Carlos: Yes - we log the routing decision with a reason code. Sometimes the auto text may say "fallback to radwood 7b" - it's transcription weirdness but the underlying field is consistent: model_id and variant.
[01:06] Oliver: And retention - how long do you keep request logs? We have strict retention policies and need to ensure PII is not stored beyond our TTL.
[01:12] Aisha: Good point. By default Hosted keeps 30 days, but for Dedicated/Private you can configure shorter retention and disable payload storage. We'll send the exact retention settings in the security pack.
[01:22] [01:20] Tom: Also thinking about encryption - KMS, HSM integration. We need customer-managed keys for some workloads.
[01:28] Carlos: Redwood supports KMS integration for Private deployments and there's a route for HSM-backed keys. Key usage and audit logs are surfaced in the Console's security tab - again we'll share the integration guide.
[01:38] Carlos: Back to the UI, error analysis view groups errors by type: model timeouts, generation truncation, invalid input, and rate limit events. You can click into a bucket to see full request logs and the trace.
[01:50] Maya: Can we attach our own alerting or export traces to our SIEM?
[01:54] Carlos: Yes - we have webhook exports for alerts and an API to stream request logs. For Dedicated there's an option to forward logs to your cloud storage or SIEM.
[02:06] [02:00] Aisha: I'm going to demo a debugging flow we ran with another customer - show how you'd triage a spike in token latency. Carlos, can you pull up the trace viewer?
[02:16] Carlos: Sure - pulling up a real example (sanitized). See here, a series of requests with increased tail latency around 11:22. The trace shows a compilation event that coincided with a model rollout.
[02:29] Carlos: We annotate the CPU/GPU kernel time (when available) and note KV cache hit rate - in this case the hit rate dropped from 92% to 20% which explains the extra token generation.
[02:41] Maya: That cache drop, is that due to sequence-length variance or batch rebalancing?
[02:45] Carlos: Looks like sequence-length - a sudden influx of longer prompts evicted the prefix cache. You can tune the cache TTL and per-route cache keys.
[02:55] [02:50] Oliver: If we wanted to reproduce this in our environment, can we point the Console to ingest our request logs and then replay?
[03:01] Carlos: Yes - we support an ingestion API. You can post request logs and traces; the Console will index them and you can run the same error analysis queries. For Private deployments ingestion can be internal-only.
[03:13] Tom: How about performance benchmarks? We want to run a realistic workload with our prompt mix and measure P95 latency and cost.
[03:19] Aisha: We'll coordinate a benchmark window. Carlos can run an assisted benchmark using your sample requests and return a report with latency, token costs, and recommended quantization/ batching settings.
[03:30] [03:30] Maya: One more security flow question - audit logs for who viewed traces and downloaded logs? We need RBAC and SSO.
[03:36] Carlos: RBAC is supported; view/download events are logged with user ID and stored in the audit logs. SSO via SAML/OIDC is supported and we can show a sample claim set.
[03:47] Aisha: Quick demo of request-log search -
[03:49] [03:48] Carlos: (screen share) Here's the Request Logs tab. You can filter by request_id, model_id, status_code, and custom route tags. We'll show a fuzzy search too - sometimes transcription labels the model as "radwood" instead of "Redwood" in older exports.
[04:05] Maya: Ha, yeah we saw that in the test CSV.
[04:08] Carlos: Note the 'Related Traces' panel - click a request and you get full trace, related requests within the same session, and a timeline view showing where errors occurred.
[04:20] [04:15] Oliver: For the ingestion API, do you accept gzipped ndjson? We generate high throughput logs.
[04:25] Carlos: We accept gzipped ndjson over HTTPS and have guidance on chunk size and backpressure. For very high throughput we recommend batching on client side and using our bulk ingestion endpoint.
[04:36] Tom: Cost question - if we stream full request payloads for debugging, does that significantly increase Hosted costs?
[04:41] Aisha: Hosting/storage of logs is a potential cost; we typically recommend storing minimal payloads and using a short TTL. For deeper debugging we can enable payload capture for a controlled window during the benchmark.
[04:53] [04:50] Maya: Any caveats about PII redaction?
[04:53] Carlos: We have built-in redaction helpers and recommend client-side redaction. For regulated data you can route to Private and keep logs in your VPC.
[05:05] Carlos: Moving on - error analysis, you can annotate a set of golden prompts and run regressions. Console will surface quality regressions tied to model versions and show token-level diffs.
[05:19] Maya: That would be super useful for evaluation. Do you support automated alerts if a regression crosses a threshold?
[05:24] Carlos: Yes, alerts can be tied to eval sets and thresholds; they can trigger webhooks or email.
[05:32] [05:30] Aisha: We're about halfway through - any urgent questions before I go into next steps?
[05:36] Tom: No, go ahead.
[05:39] Aisha: Great. Recap and actions: we'll send the security pack with SOC2 and KMS/HSM notes, Carlos will share the ingestion runbook and we'll schedule the benchmark. Tom, you'll share sample request IDs.
[05:52] [06:00] Tom: Sounds good, we'll aim to send samples by end of next week.
[06:05] Maya: One more small ask - can you include a short doc on recommended batching settings for P95 optimization?
[06:11] Carlos: Yep, I'll include a recommended config based on your target p95 and token budget - note that sometimes auto-batching can increase tail latency if not tuned.
[06:21] Aisha: Any competitive concerns to call out? We often get questions on model coverage vs Anthropic/OpenAI and custom self-hosted stacks. For observability specifically customers compare how deep kernel timing and KV cache stats are surfaced.
[06:37] Oliver: That's one of our evaluation metrics - depth of telemetry.
[06:40] [06:45] Aisha: Alright, final notes: follow-ups will include pricing, security docs and the bench window. Thank you all for your time.
[06:53] Tom: Thanks Aisha, Carlos. Appreciate the walkthrough.
[06:56] Maya: Thanks.
[06:58] Carlos: Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: minor auto-caption errors present (e.g., "radwood" for "Redwood", "K V cache" tokenization). The transcript was trimmed for concision but preserves key timestamps and troubleshooting flow.
